title: Elastic rendezvous broker for heterogeneous prefill/decode scheduling and kernel steering
creator: Liam Chen
description: Add an 'elastic rendezvous broker' that coordinates rendezvous timing, kernel selection hints, and opportunistic NCCL piggybacking across heterogeneous GPU groups to reduce prefill stalls and tail latency during mixed prefill/decode workloads. The broker will observe hardware capabilities, per-request sequence-length distributions, and KV-cache hit patterns to decide whether to: 1) align rendezvous windows across subset of devices, 2) defer less-critical comms for overlap, or 3) trigger kernel-hedging on slow hosts. This feature targets multi-tenant Dedicated and Private deployments where device heterogeneity and variable request mixtures cause tail latency spikes.
acceptance_criteria: Broker can dynamically form rendezvous groups and achieve >=15% reduction in 99th percentile prefill latency on heterogeneous clusters compared to baseline.
Kernel steering hooks expose hints to runtime kernel selector with <1ms decision latency and do not violate existing SLOs.
NCCL piggybacking reduces inter-node small-message overhead without increasing average latency by >5%.
End-to-end regression tests and integration benchmarks committed, with at least one Canary rollout plan documented in Console playbook.
progress_updates: 2025-11-13: Spike completed to collect rendezvous timing distribution across 6 heterogeneous clusters; found 30-120ms variance correlated with device type and NVLink topology.

2025-11-18: Design review with infra and runtime teams; decided broker will run as control-plane microservice collocated with conductor, exposing 'rendezvous plan' via lightweight protobuf; runtime will consume plan via gRPC cache.

2025-11-22: Prototype implemented: broker can form variable-size groups and instruct two strategies: immediate-aligned and opportunistic-defer. Microbenchmarks show 10% p99 improvement on one testbed.
2025-11-28: Discovered regression where opportunistic-defer increases decode tail under high-concurrency; added heuristics to detect decode-heavy windows and disable defer for that job class.
2025-12-03: End-to-end test harness added to CI; starting first internal canary against dedicated-dev cluster (canary-3).
design_decisions: Broker runs out-of-band to avoid adding per-token latency inside hot path.
Use hint-based kernel steering rather than forcing kernel changes; runtime retains final authority to select kernel variant.
Favor smaller rendezvous groups to reduce blocking across slow hosts; enable optional 'temporary coalescing' when many short prefills detected.
NCCL piggybacking implemented as opportunistic coalesced allreduce for small control-plane messages rather than mixing with large-value comms to avoid head-of-line-blocking.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Broker misclassifies workload leading to worse tail latency. Mitigation: conservative defaults, phased rollout, and automatic fallback to per-request local scheduling.
Risk: gRPC control-plane adds instability. Mitigation: keep messages idempotent, add watchers in runtime to fall back to cached last-good plan.
Risk: Kernel hinting may interfere with future kernel-selection experiments. Mitigation: add opt-in header flags and telemetry to correlate hints with kernel choice and outcomes.
testing_plan: Unit tests for broker group logic and policy decisions.
Simulated multi-tenant workload replay with mixed short/long prefills to validate heuristics.
Cluster-level soak test for 48 hours with gradual traffic ramp and automatic rollback on SLO deviation.
Telemetry ingestion to track kernel-hint adoption and per-host rendezvous latency metrics.
review_feedback: PM (Caroline Ortiz): Emphasize safe defaults and clear opt-out for enterprise customers concerned about reproducibility.
Design (Arjun Rao): Request that UI expose rendezvous-group formation events in Console for debugging.
Infra (Sasha Ivanov): Favor lightweight protobuf over JSON for control messages to minimize serialization overhead.
Security (Priya Menon): Ensure broker-to-runtime auth uses short-lived mTLS certs; added security_review_required flag.
notes: Follow-up: evaluate synergy with KV cache prefetcher to further reduce prefill volume.
Future work: expose API for customers to declare latency vs cost preference so broker can optimize per-tenant.
